name: Kirchberg in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Premier year-round resort in the Brixen Valley with direct KitzSki access, the pristine Spertental, and the UNESCO Antlassritt tradition.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kirchberg in Tirol is located at an altitude of 837 metres in the heart of the Brixental within the district of Kitzbühel. Cradled by the rolling grass-covered mountains of the Kitzbühel Alps and just six kilometres west of Kitzbühel itself, this vibrant market town of approximately 5,350 residents ranks among Tyrol's foremost holiday destinations. Branching southward is the scenic Spertental valley leading to the mountaineering village of Aschau, shadowed by towering limestone crags including the Großer Rettenstein at 2,366 metres. Kirchberg artfully marries top-tier alpine sports infrastructure with an authentic Tyrolean village spirit. Whether serving as a gateway to the KitzSki winter paradise, a summertime hiking haven, or the setting for cherished folk traditions, Kirchberg delights outdoor enthusiasts and families throughout all four seasons.

History

The town was first documented in 1241 under the name 'Chirchperch'. In 1377, the Bishop of Chiemsee acquired the local estates, maintaining administration under the Archbishopric of Salzburg until secularization in 1803, with Kirchberg officially joining Tyrol in 1816. During the sixteenth century, the town flourished through silver and copper mining on Mount Gaisberg. A celebrated historical episode gave rise to the legendary Brixentaler Antlassritt: during the Thirty Years' War in 1643, local Brixen Valley farmers repelled Swedish troops at the narrow Klausenbach defile. In gratitude, a ceremonial horseback procession has taken place every Corpus Christi, with hundreds of decorated riders riding from Kirchberg to the Swedish Chapel in Klausen—a custom inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. The Baroque Parish Church of Saint Ulrich was erected in 1736 by master builder Jakob Singer and thoughtfully extended in the 1980s by Clemens Holzmeister.

Getting There

Motorists arrive via the Inntal Autobahn A12, exiting at Wörgl-Ost and continuing along the B170 Brixental Federal Highway through Hopfgarten and Westendorf directly into Kirchberg. Travelling from Salzburg or Munich, access is also available toll-free via Kufstein, St. Johann in Tirol, and Kitzbühel. Rail travellers enjoy outstanding links: the Kirchberg in Tirol railway station is a key stop along the Salzburg-Tyrol Railway, served regularly by ÖBB Regional-Express trains, S-Bahn line S8, and international EuroCity services. Across the Brixental valley, a well-synchronized regional bus and complimentary ski bus system guarantees effortless transit.

Tips

In winter, Kirchberg provides seamless access to 233 kilometres of groomed slopes in the KitzSki area via the ten-seater Fleckalmbahn, Maierlbahn, and the Ki-West gondola, connecting onward to the SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser - Brixental. The local Gaisberg mountain boasts a floodlit 3.5-kilometre natural toboggan run and night skiing. In summer, the Gaisberg transforms into a mountain biking paradise featuring the celebrated Lisi Osl Flow Trail. Hikers love journeying into the pristine Spertental valley to visit the Kasplatzl show dairy at the foot of the Großer Rettenstein for artisanal alpine cheeses. On hot summer afternoons, the Kirchberg bathing lake offers heated pools and expansive sunbathing lawns.
